referents.why: 'his heart' is a third masculine singular possessor; the one whose heart is hardened is Pharaoh, the subject of 'he saw'.
referents.category: possessor in the subject's own act

referents.why: 'would not listen to them' is masculine plural: Moses and Aaron, the composite the refusal is aimed at.
the subject of 'would not listen' is Pharaoh, the subject of the seeing and the hardening.
referents.category: implied subject of a narrative clause

links.why: 'saw that there was relief': cl1 is what Pharaoh saw, the object of the seeing.
links.category: that-clause after a verb of perceiving

links.why: ka'asher with a qatal saying: the refusal is just as the LORD had said, so the action is declared the fulfilment of an earlier word.
cl1 is what cl0 saw, the object of the seeing, not an event before it. cl0 begins the verse.
a separate waw on the infinitive absolute: the hardening follows the seeing. The sense does not make the seeing a cause, so it stays a plain and.
a hardened will and then the refusal that follows is the R4 example of a result, not a plain and.
the hardening of the heart brings about the refusal to listen.
links.category: state then what it brings about
